best_field_traits: Introduced cultivated cereal, generally annual with fibrous roots rather than a perennial knotty rhizome.
Stout erect stems and comparatively broad foliage, often around 6–20 mm wide.
Dense heavy terminal foxtail head, often about 5–30 cm long; shape varies with cultivated form.
Bristles are modified sterile branchlets below spikelets, not grass floret awns.
Field plant may reflect selected cultivars/hybrids; species concept and origin distinguish it from indigenous bristlegrasses.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Full robust plant beside human scale, including stem bases
Whole mature thick head in side profile with scale
Leaf collar/ligule and broad leaf with ruler
Separated mature spikelet and associated bristles with mm scale
Belowground fibrous root system; no claim without photo
crew_field_check: Count bristles under 10× magnification; these are reduced branches, NOT true awns.
Measure whole flowering head and a mature spikelet.
Inspect the base/collar/rhizomes on the SAME PLANT; do not force identification from a single image.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. parviflora is a rhizomatous perennial with knotty rootstock and several bristles per spikelet. S. scheelei is a perennial with long bottlebrush-like flowering heads but much less milletlike bulky crop habit. S. reverchonii has a thin, often interrupted head with very sparse short bristles, not the densely packed foxtail-millet head. S. viridis can also make a foxtail seedhead; look for the annual cultivated giant millet architecture and confirm mature spikelets.
